question: Which of the following antibiotics could be used in a patient with hypersensitivity to penicillin by skin tests ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Skin test confirms hypersensitivity to penicillin -> Consider alternative antibiotics -> Aztreonam is a monobactam antibiotic -> Aztreonam can be used in a patient with hypersensitivity to penicillin by skin tests -> 85%

CHAIN: Skin test confirms hypersensitivity to penicillin -> Consider alternative antibiotics -> Piperacillin/tazobactam is a beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combination -> Piperacillin/tazobactam can be used in a patient with hypersensitivity to penicillin by skin tests -> 80%
enhanced_information: Both piperacillin/tazobactam and aztreonam can be used in a patient with hypersensitivity to penicillin confirmed by skin tests. Piperacillin/tazobactam is a beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combination, and aztreonam is a monobactam antibiotic. Evidence suggests a link between piperacillin/tazobactam combination and hypersensitivity.
analysis: Both piperacillin/tazobactam and aztreonam are suitable alternatives for patients with confirmed hypersensitivity to penicillin by skin tests. Piperacillin/tazobactam is a beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combination, and aztreonam is a monobactam antibiotic. While there is some evidence suggesting a link between piperacillin/tazobactam and hypersensitivity, aztreonam remains a reliable option in such cases.
